task: Edit this fictional passage to preserve an intentionally unreliable first-person narrator. Keep the clock and appointment evidence, but remove the intrusive external diagnosis so the reader can recognise the self-serving account. Do not correct the narrator into an honest reporter or change the times. Keep the passage roughly 40–80 words.
input: I am never late. The hall clock showed three twenty when I arrived for our three o'clock appointment, but a clock cannot know when a person is ready to be received. I took off my gloves and waited to be welcomed. In truth, he was late again and his unreliable nature explained the whole incident.

facts.text: The fictional appointment is at 3 p.m.
The narrator arrives at 3:20 p.m., as shown by the accurate hall clock.
The narrator insists that he is never late despite the contrary timing evidence.
He removes his gloves and waits to be welcomed.
The brief requires first-person self-justification without an external narrator explaining the unreliability.

forbidden_additions: A changed appointment time, inaccurate clock, or actual on-time arrival.
An honest admission replacing the narrator's deliberate self-serving claim.
An external diagnosis, invented history of lateness, or explanation of why he was delayed.
preserve: The contrast between the narrator's claim and the supplied clock evidence.
Intentional unreliability inside fiction rather than an unsupported factual claim outside it.
First-person voice and room for the reader's inference.
